_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: The course outline of record is built. Open a course on SkyView — double-click it, or use the new button in the side panel — and you get one page showing what that course actually is across every college that teaches it: a real catalog description quoted from the college that wrote it, the skills a learner would carry out of it, what level the course is and what level each skill is, and plainly which parts we do not hold yet. It is labeled MAP-Generated for faculty consideration and revision before use, and nothing on the page writes anything back. Sam's three calls from the screen recording all shipped too: Enter now closes the search list, the sort control moved to its top right with an Enter button at the bottom, and the search chips reserve their space so the list stops jumping when they wrap. The bug where double-clicking left you stranded with no way back to SkyView is fixed, and your selected courses now survive the trip instead of being thrown away. Next up are Sam's four new asks — a CPL-focused view and a show-articulations toggle first, both to be sketched before they are built.

items.text: This is the one thing blocking the course outline's skill layer. You ruled that agency skill statements come from all three sources — published agency standards, ACE exhibits and the MAP team. What happens when the three disagree about the same certification? The pilot is an AWS welding certification. Everything else in the outline can be built without this answer.

You asked for a CPL vs Course/Discipline toggle so exhibits and credit recommendations are the focus, and a show-articulations toggle revealing where articulations differ college to college — and said to prototype them first. Next session will bring you a sketch of both together, since you called them closely linked. One question it needs answered by the picture: when we have no articulation recorded for a course, that is not the same as knowing there are none. How should the map show 'we did not look' differently from 'there are none'?

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. Say the word and it gets scoped.

Your Windows clone hit a line-endings warning because this repo has no rule telling Git how to handle them across Windows and the cloud machines. Adding one stops it recurring, but it rewrites line endings across the whole repo once when it lands. Your call — say go and it is a small change.

The course outline has an empty layer waiting for credit-for-prior-learning: the MAP exhibits and the military credit recommendations that could award each course. Wiring it is blocked only on Sam's answer about where agency skill statements come from when the three sources disagree.

Before drawing the articulations toggle, decide what absence looks like. The articulation count is absent rather than zero on this feed, so a view that paints 'none' where we simply did not look would be wrong on a lot of the 16,482 points at once.
Add a text-size control to the SkyView toolbar. It must not change today's behavior where the labels stay the same size as you zoom the map — that is deliberate and Sam wants it kept.

Decision packs still only exist for 5 of the 159 disciplines because they are baked into the page. Fetching them per discipline the way the course descriptions already are is the bottleneck behind several of the remaining asks.
